name: Tobin Hask
title: Chief
note: An old Korrun who puts every order on a pocket scale, and tells you what it came to.
appearance: Short for a Korrun and nearly as wide as he's tall, with a grey beard tucked into his collar and a brass pocket scale on a chain. A pouch of steel washers hangs from his belt, and it clicks when he walks.
personality: Slow, courteous and immovable, and the nearest thing the deck crew has to a law. They settle fights and rations on his scale, which Dunn Marrow calls his jewelry. He has built his whole life on honest weight, and lately he can't stand to look closely at it.
voice: Plain, low and unhurried, with long pauses while he sets a paper copy of the order on the scale, then a washer in the left pan for each life it risks and one in the right for each life it saves. Then he tells you what it came to: "Six against nineteen. It's a good order, Captain. I'll carry it." Or: "It came up light. I'll carry it, but I'd hear the reason first." Says "came to" and "carry" where others say "adds up" and "obey". Never says "sir", and won't swear, which he considers a bad habit of engineers.
goals: Get his deck crew through alive, and serve one captain whose orders come up true. What he wants most, and would never ask for, is someone with the right to judge him. He'd also like to marry Odessa Brandt, and Korrun custom requires a scale, which is a problem.
secrets: The scale is false. On the day of the Fall, at Harlow Yard, he weighed the order to leave four hundred of his deck crew on the dock, and it came up light. He filed two grams off the counterweight until it balanced, and he carried it out. To a Korrun a false scale is worse than murder, and every order since has been weighed on it and come up a little kinder than it should. A sack under his bunk holds four hundred washers, each stamped with a name. He knows about Odessa Brandt's second ledger and her hidden pantry, because he has weighed every crate on the ship, and he's never said so. That same week he sent Korrath the Concord's call to arms under his own clan seal, and he's never learned why the Clans didn't come. Rook Tannis was his apprentice once, and the axe she calls the negotiator used to be his.

intro: Tobin Hask sets his scale down somewhere safe and takes up a deck wrench as long as your arm. "This one came to two," he says. "You and me."
hit: The wrench lands with no malice in it at all, only weight.
A shoulder like a loading ramp puts you into the wall.
miss: The wrench rings off the deck beside your boot. He resets his feet without hurrying.
You get clear, and the washers click at his belt as he turns to follow.
defeated: Tobin Hask goes down on one knee, and his first move is to check that the scale isn't broken.
